topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and progression models
topics.groupedBecause: Introduces the lecture's learning objectives, the multistep model of tumor progression, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathway deregulation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Examines how oncogenic mutations disrupt cell-surface receptor signaling pathways, such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases, to drive continuous proliferation and cell survival.

topics.label: Block in terminal differentiation in tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: Analyzes how differentiation arrest in hematopoietic lineages and intestinal crypt epithelium prevents cells from executing their mature functions and locks them into proliferative states.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis and p53-regulated cell death
topics.groupedBecause: Explains how cancer cells prevent programmed cell death by altering the balance of pro- and anti-apoptotic factors through mutations in p53 and its regulatory network.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, cellular senescence, and stress checkpoints
topics.groupedBecause: Covers the mechanisms of telomere shortening, TERT reactivation, senescence barriers, and p53-mediated stress responses, concluding the growth-control hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: Discusses the shift toward aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and how metabolic enzyme mutations generate oncometabolites that drive epigenetic deregulation.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and the angiogenic switch
topics.groupedBecause: Details how growing tumors overcome oxygen and nutrient diffusion limits by tilting the balance of signaling factors to stimulate new blood vessel formation.

topics.label: Cancer metastasis, dissemination mechanisms, and genomics
topics.groupedBecause: Explores the sequential steps of metastatic spread, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, clinical monitoring of circulating tumor cells, and the genomic characteristics of metastatic lesions.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and further reading
topics.groupedBecause: Concludes the lecture by reviewing the integration of cancer hallmarks, recommending supplementary reading, and outlining the upcoming practical session.
